subject: Pricing exhibit: commit buffer & safeguard appendix — proposed compromise and redline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, contracts@atlashealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing exhibit: commit buffer & safeguard appendix — proposed language & next steps

Hi Sinead / Atlas procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive sync yesterday. Attached is the draft Order Form with the pricing exhibit and the commit-buffer language we discussed. High level summary of the proposal we shared: 

- A rolling monthly "commit buffer" equal to 15% of committed monthly tokens that protects against small overage spikes without triggering a true-up.
- A safeguard (floor) that ensures baseline economics for both parties if usage drops below 70% of committed monthly volume.
- Quarterly true-up cadence; 30-day notice for any catch-up invoices.

Ask: please review the attached OrderForm_Redwood_Atlas_Pricing_Exhibit_v1.docx and send redlines back by EOD Friday 5/19 if possible so we can route to legal. If you prefer, send a short list of open points and we can align in a 30-minute call.

Attachments: OrderForm_Redwood_Atlas_Pricing_Exhibit_v1.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sinead O'Connor <sinead.o@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Marta Legal <marta.legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: commit buffer & safeguard appendix — redlines attached

Karthik —

Thanks for sending. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the draft and attached a redline (Atlas_Redline_OrderForm_v1_redline.pdf). Primary concerns:

1) Minimums / Floor: the 70% floor as written still leaves material downside to Atlas in a prolonged ramp-down scenario. We proposed a tiered floor that steps to 80% for the first 3 months after any material reduction and then reverts to 70% thereafter.

2) Buffer mechanics: your 15% static buffer is workable for predictable workloads but not for our seasonal spikes. We redlined language asking for a percentage-based buffer tied to a trailing 3-month median and a cap on per-event spikes (we propose 30% cap).

3) True-up cadence & timing: procurement wants monthly true-ups for visibility, but legal is concerned about administrative churn. We proposed a monthly reporting cadence with quarterly invoiced true-ups (i.e., report monthly, bill quarterly).

4) Emergency surge carveout: we asked to add an explicit "stability carveout" for declared emergency incidents where Atlas traffic spikes for no more than 14 days and are not chargeable against committed bandwidth.

We're open to a compromise but need clearer guardrails. Also, please confirm whether Redwood can accept a 60-day net term for any catch-up invoices as a special concession for this deal.

Attaching: Atlas_Redline_OrderForm_v1_redline.pdf

Best,
Sinead O'Connor
Head of Vendor Procurement
Atlas Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sinead O'Connor <sinead.o@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Marta Legal <marta.legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: commit buffer & safeguard appendix — proposed compromise (redline attached)

Sinead / Marta / team —

Thanks for the thoughtful redline. We read it with our product & legal teams overnight and propose the following compromise to close the trade-offs you called out:

- Floor: accept a tiered floor as you proposed but limit the higher 80% step to a 3-month transition window only when Atlas requests a deliberate contract downsize (i.e., when Atlas elects to reduce committed volumes). This protects Redwood against abrupt planned downsizes while still giving Atlas short-term relief.

- Buffer mechanics: move from a static 15% to a hybrid model — a trailing 3M median-based buffer with a hard per-event cap of 30%. We also add a "predictability adjustment": if Atlas provides a 14-day rolling forecast that shows >20% variance vs median we will temporarily waive the per-event cap for declared planned events with 7 days notice.

- True-ups: agree to monthly reporting with quarterly invoiced true-ups. For administrative simplicity, we'll provide a one-page reconciliation workbook each month.

- Stability carveout: accept a 14-day emergency carveout for declared incidents (mutually agreed), with a limit of 3 carveouts per 12-month period.

- Payment terms: Redwood can accept a 60-day net term on catch-up invoices for this renewal provided the overall contract keeps standard 30-day net for recurring invoices.

I've attached our proposed redline (Redwood_Pricing_Proposed_Amend_v2.docx) with exact language for each bullet. Key asks from our side:
- No retroactive changes to already-invoiced months unless both parties explicitly agree in writing.
- Add a short reconciliation SLA: Atlas has 30 days to dispute any true-up invoice or it becomes payable.

If this looks acceptable I suggest we exchange redlines in DocuSign next week and target signature before the end of May. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to run the redline line-by-line if that helps.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Proposed_Amend_v2.docx

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sinead O'Connor <sinead.o@atlashealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: commit buffer & safeguard appendix — proposed compromise

Sinead / team —

Karthik's proposal aligns with our commercial flex and the legal trade-offs we can take on. Two quick notes from the broader commercial team: 

1) DocuSign timing: can Atlas commit to a 3-business-day review window once the final redline is shared via DocuSign? We need to land this by May 31 to meet our internal provisioning timeline for dedicated capacity.

2) One narrow request on the no-retroactivity point: please allow a single controlled exception for billing corrections discovered in a monthly reconciliation (limited to 90 days lookback and not to exceed $10k per calendar year) — this is just to fix obvious accounting errors and won't be used to reopen commercial terms.

If you can confirm those two items we'll accept the compromise and I'll instruct legal to prepare the final DocuSign packet.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
